previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with a history of liver transplant for HCV cirrhosis, chronic kidney disease, and diabetes was admitted due to a three-week history of non-bloody, mucus-containing diarrhea and dehydration. Her creatinine rose from a baseline of 1.6–2.0 to 2.2, indicating acute on chronic kidney injury, likely pre-renal from fluid loss. She was treated with IV fluids and albumin, leading to improvement in renal function with creatinine decreasing to 1.2 by discharge. Diarrhea resolved during the hospitalization. Stool studies were negative for C. diff, bacterial pathogens, CMV, Giardia, and parasites, though one O&P remained pending. Tacrolimus level was initially elevated at 5.6 but decreased to 3.8 with dose management. Her Lasix and nadolol were held temporarily due to kidney concerns and nadolol was restarted upon improvement. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with hepatology for pending test results, tacrolimus monitoring, and guidance on restarting Lasix.
problems: HCV cirrhosis c/b HCC s/p liver transplant c/b recurrent HCV, ascites, grade II esophageal varices
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus

Lower Thorax: Limited views of the lung bases are clear.  There is a small
right pleural effusion.

steatosis.  Note is made of parenchymal atrophy at the periphery of the
transplant liver.  Tiny T2 hyperintense lesion in the left lobe without
enhancement likely represent a cyst or biliary hamartoma.  No suspicious focal
liver lesion is seen.  There is mild periportal edema.  The portal vein is
patent.  There is early filling of the anterior branch of the right portal
vein during the arterial phase likely due to an arterio-portal fistula
(14:36). Gastroesophageal varices are noted.

extrahepatic bile ducts, this is likely due to donor and recipient duct
caliber mismatch rather than true obstruction.  No filling defect or stricture
is seen within the bile ducts.  The gallbladder is surgically absent.

Pancreas: The pancreas is atrophic but demonstrates normal signal intensity. 
There is no main duct dilatation or peripancreatic abnormality.

normal in size.  Small susceptibility artifact within the spleen is likely due
to calcification versus gamna gandy body.

nonenhancing lesions are identified cortically compatible with simple cysts.

are unremarkable without dilatation or bowel wall thickening.

likely reactive.

middle hepatic veins are patent.  The right and left hepatic arteries are
patent.  Major intra-abdominal branches are patent.

Soft tissue structures are grossly unremarkable.

obstruction.
